findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed using bare hands to grab cooked bacon before being added to a serving plate. The activity was ceased and corrected. The employee discarded the bacon and made sure to use gloves when handling ready-to-eat (RTE) foods. Ensure that RTE foods are handled with either utensils or gloved hands.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The employee bathroom lacked paper towel for handwashing. Discussed with the PIC and paper towels were provided to the handsink. Ensure that all handsinks are equipped with running warm water, hand soap, and paper towels to be sure that hands are getting washed effectively.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There wasn't any hand soap available in the employee bathroom. Discussed with the PIC and hand-soap was provided to correct the violation. Be sure that every hand-sink has a supply of soap to ensure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Several Time/Temperature Control foods (TCS) stored on the steam table were probed between 91F - 96F. These foods included mashed potatoes, green beans, corn, shredded pork, etc. The foods were placed on the steam table no longer than two hours prior to the inspection. Foods were reheated on the stove to at least 165F to correct the violation. The water inside of the steam table was probed to ensure that the table was working properly (probed 175F). Ensure that TCS foods are always hot held at 135F or above to maintain proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed there to be soil build-up on the blade of the can opener. Discussed with PIC. PIC had the can opener cleaned immediately in the dish machine. Ensure the can opener is cleaned regularly enough to keep it clean. COS
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.
